title: MTH 102 — Elementary Mathematics II: Calculus
overview: This study pack covers foundational differential and integral calculus — limits, derivatives, and basic integration — essential mathematical tools used throughout engineering analysis.

modules.title: Limits and Differentiation
modules.summary:
A limit describes the value a function approaches as its input approaches a certain value, forming the conceptual foundation of calculus. Derivatives measure the instantaneous rate of change of a function — geometrically, the slope of the tangent line at a given point.

Basic differentiation rules include the power rule (d/dx[xⁿ] = nxⁿ⁻¹), the constant rule (derivative of a constant is zero), and the sum rule (derivative of a sum is the sum of derivatives). These rules allow differentiation of polynomial functions directly, without needing to compute limits from first principles each time.

Derivatives have direct engineering applications: velocity is the derivative of displacement with respect to time, and acceleration is the derivative of velocity with respect to time.
keyPoints: A limit describes the value a function approaches as input approaches a specific value
A derivative measures the instantaneous rate of change (slope of the tangent line)
Constant Rule: the derivative of a constant is zero
Velocity = derivative of displacement; Acceleration = derivative of velocity

definitions.definition: The value that a function approaches as its input approaches a specific value.
A measure of how a function's output changes as its input changes; geometrically, the slope of the tangent line at a point.
The differentiation rule stating that d/dx[xⁿ] = nxⁿ⁻¹.
A straight line that touches a curve at a single point, having the same slope as the curve at that point.

workedExamples.title: Applying the Power Rule
steps: Differentiate each term separately using the power rule

workedExamples.title: Finding Velocity from a Displacement Function
workedExamples.problem: The displacement of a particle is given by s(t) = 2t³ - 3t² + 4t. Find the velocity function.
steps: Velocity is the derivative of displacement with respect to time: v(t) = ds/dt

quiz.question: What does a derivative measure geometrically?
options: The slope of the tangent line at a point
quiz.explanation: A derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change, which geometrically corresponds to the slope of the tangent line at that point.

quiz.question: According to the Power Rule, what is d/dx[x⁵]?
quiz.explanation: The Power Rule states d/dx[xⁿ] = nxⁿ⁻¹, so d/dx[x⁵] = 5x⁴.

modules.title: Basic Integration
modules.summary:
Integration is the reverse process of differentiation, used to find a function given its derivative, and to calculate quantities like area under a curve. Indefinite integration produces a general function plus a constant of integration (C), since the derivative of any constant is zero.

The power rule for integration states: ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C, valid for n ≠ -1. Definite integrals, evaluated between two limits, calculate the exact area under a curve between those bounds, and don't include a constant of integration since it cancels out.

Integration has direct engineering applications: displacement is the integral of velocity with respect to time, connecting back to the differentiation relationships covered earlier.
keyPoints: Integration is the reverse process of differentiation
Indefinite integration includes a constant of integration, C
Power Rule for integration: ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C (for n ≠ -1)
Definite integrals calculate the exact area under a curve between two bounds
Displacement = integral of velocity with respect to time

definitions.definition: The mathematical process of finding a function from its derivative, or calculating area under a curve.
An arbitrary constant added to the result of an indefinite integral, since differentiation of any constant yields zero.
The general antiderivative of a function, expressed with a constant of integration C.
An integral evaluated between two specific limits, giving a numerical value representing area under a curve.

workedExamples.title: Finding an Indefinite Integral
steps: Apply the power rule for integration to each term

workedExamples.title: Evaluating a Definite Integral
steps: Find the indefinite integral: ∫3x² dx = x³

quiz.question: What is added to the result of an indefinite integral, and why?
options: A variable, because the answer is incomplete
A constant of integration (C), since the derivative of a constant is zero
A coefficient based on the power
quiz.explanation: Since differentiating any constant gives zero, the original function could have had any constant term — this is represented by C.

quiz.question: What does a definite integral calculate?
options: The exact area under a curve between two limits
The slope at a single point
quiz.explanation: A definite integral, evaluated between two bounds, gives the exact numerical area under the curve within those limits.
